<reason>PRO (B) won a clear but competitive debate. A's strongest route was burden-shifting: the motion requires justifying a net increase in the mid-budget tier, and alternatives (microbudgets, acquisitions, selective originals) could renew the slate more cheaply. A pressed this well in pressure questions and answered B's questions honestly with clean A1/A2 labels. But B answered both pressures substantively: underinvestment is shown by the pattern (tier collapsed while audiences demonstrably show up for original horror/comedy when made), and mid-budget production is the only renewal mechanism operating at scale — microbudgets are rare lightning strikes and acquisitions pay someone else's markup. A's rebuttal 2 (frequency-vs-budget, acquisitions buy information) was a partial answer but never fully neutralized the scale argument. Meanwhile B landed the decisive crystallization: A conceded originals renew the slate, franchises degrade, and mega-sequels can be ruinous, leaving A defending "value renewal without moving the dollar" — a description of the status quo that produced the collapse. B's "what changes?" closing framed the choice memorably; A's closing restated the burden gap without resolving the status-quo problem. B's opening had minor grounding wobbles (Harry Potter as an ungambled original, Paranormal Activity stretched into a $15-30M frame), which A exploited, but these did not break B's portfolio case. Both sides showed good discipline and format compliance; B made the debate easier to decide.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's second rebuttal (B4.3-B4.6): the direct answer that mid-budget production is the only at-scale renewal mechanism — volume, portfolio effects, and talent pipeline that microbudgets and acquisitions cannot provide — combined with the turn that all of CON's alternatives are ways of avoiding the commitment the motion describes. A's B4-counter on frequency-vs-budget and information-buying partially blunted it, but the "every remedy they named is what studios already claim to do" frame survived and decided the closing exchange.</best_rebuttal>
